title: Scalar-extension maps form morphisms of distinguished triangles
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Write $D(R)$ and $D(S)$ for the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of their abelian categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $Q_R,Q_S$ for localization from homotopy categories. Let $F=-\otimes_R^LS:D(R)\to D(S)$ be the exact derived scalar-extension functor computed by K-flat resolutions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Let $U:D(S)\to D(R)$ be termwise restriction of scalars along $\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; use its exact derived functor, computed termwise, with the unchanged underlying abelian sheaves [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Give these functors their canonical shift structures from the complexes, using $(P[1])^i=P^{i+1}$ and $d_{P[1]}=-d_P$ [def-weil-triangulated-category].

There is a canonical natural transformation $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{D(R)}\to UF$ with the following characterization. For every complex $C$ and every K-flat resolution $p:P\to C$, under the canonical identification $F(Q_RC)\cong Q_S(P\otimes_R S)$, its component is represented by the roof
$$Q_RC\xleftarrow{\ Q_Rp\ }Q_RP\xrightarrow{\ Q_R i_P\ }UQ_S(P\otimes_R S),\qquad i_P(x)=x\otimes1.$$
This characterization is independent of the resolution. If $\chi_X:UF(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(UF X)[1]$ is the composite canonical shift comparison, then
$$\chi_X\circ\eta_{X[1]}=\eta_X[1]$$
for every $X\in D(R)$. For every distinguished triangle $\Delta=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$, the three components $(\eta_X,\eta_Y,\eta_Z)$ give a morphism of distinguished triangles $\Delta\to UF(\Delta)$, with connecting square
$$\chi_X\circ UF(w)\circ\eta_Z=\eta_X[1]\circ w.$$
No flatness of $S$ over $R$, boundedness, constructibility, or existence of points of the site is assumed.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary coefficient natural transformation sectionwise using the module extension/restriction adjunction unit followed by module sheafification. Naturality follows from naturality of the two units. Prove restriction exact by reflecting finite limits and colimits with toSheaf; establish preservation of colimits by toSheaf using its compatibility with module sheafification.

Apply the specified-counit computation theorem to obtain F.IsTriangulated and invertibility of epsilon at every K-flat complex. Use K-flat resolutions and the general coefficient-map descent theorem to obtain eta, its counit comparison on every complex, and its shift equation.

For p:P -> K a K-flat resolution take c = inv(F(Qp)) followed by epsilon_P. Naturality of eta at Qp and cancellation give the required roof equation. For two transformations satisfying the roof predicate, use the same resolution: the counit equation forces their comparison c to agree. Cancel Qp, derived restriction of c, and the restriction factorization. Localization extensionality then identifies the transformations.

The composite F followed by derived restriction preserves distinguished triangles. Its triangle morphism has eta at each of its three vertices. The first two squares are naturality; naturality at the third arrow followed by the already obtained shift equation is precisely the connecting square.
